raw_case_text: A 68-year-old male presented with a 2.0x0.7 cm crusted keratotic plaque on his left infraorbital area that was concerning for nonmelanoma skin cancer. An H&E-stained section of a shave-biopsy revealed granulomatous inflammation with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and a few yeast with narrow-based budding suggestive of H. capsulatum. Urine testing for H. capsulatum antigen was negative. This lesion resolved within 2 weeks without medical intervention. Chest radiographs revealed small minimally calcified lymph nodes in the inferior right hilum and subcarinal chain (Fig. 1). One year later, the patient presented with recurrence of the lesion as a 2.0x1.0 cm thin, irritated, erythematous and crusted plaque (Fig. 2). No preceding trauma nor recent change in health status nor medications were reported. A full-skin examination demonstrated no similar lesions. Repeat biopsy was performed and showed findings similar to those previously described; however, numerous yeast forms were noted in this specimen (Fig. 3a, b). The organisms were highlighted by periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) and Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stains (Fig. 3c, d). Negative Fontana-Masson and mucicarmine stains excluded the presence of a Cryptococcus sp. Overall, the morphological appearance and the results of the special histological stains were consistent with those expected for H. capsulatum infection. Extensive microbiological testing, including Histoplasma H and M bands via immunodiffusion, urine Histoplasma antigen, Histoplasma mycelia complement fixation, Histoplasma yeast complement fixation, serum Blastomyces antigen and antibody, serum Aspergillus antibody, serum Coccidian antibody, and serum HIV antibodies and antigens were unrevealing. Cultivation of an aetiological agent was hampered by mishandling of the specimen prior to its receipt by the laboratory. A respiratory culture was not performed given significant delays in scheduling. Next-generation nucleic acid sequencing (NGS) of a 230 bp region of the internal transcribed spacer (ITS) that was amplified from the tissue block confirmed the presence of H. capsulatum. NGS was performed using an iSeq100 system (Illumina). Sequence data were analysed using an online database (ITS metagenomics app v. 1.1.0 at BaseSpace Sequence Hub). The patient was prescribed and started treatment with 200 mg itraconazole daily for a duration of 1 year and, to date, he has not reported recrudescence of the infection 8 months following his second biopsy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 68-year-old immunocompetent male presented with a recurrent 2.0 x 1.0 cm irritated, erythematous, crusted keratotic plaque on his left infraorbital cheek 1 year after spontaneous resolution of a similar biopsied lesion at the same site.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient initially presented with a 2.0 x 0.7 cm crusted keratotic plaque on the left infraorbital skin clinically suspected to be nonmelanoma skin cancer; shave biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation with rare narrow-based budding yeasts, and the lesion resolved spontaneously within 2 weeks. One year later, without intervening trauma, illness, or medication changes, the lesion recurred at the exact same site as a 2.0 x 1.0 cm thin, irritated, erythematous crusted plaque.
subjective.past_medical_history: Immunocompetent male with no systemic symptoms, trauma, or immunosuppressive medications.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive only for the localized left infraorbital skin plaque; negative for respiratory or constitutional symptoms.

objective.physical_examination: A solitary 2.0 x 1.0 cm thin, irritated, erythematous, crusted keratotic plaque on the left infraorbital cheek; full-body skin examination showed no other lesions.
objective.routine_investigations: Chest radiograph showed small, minimally calcified right inferior hilar and subcarinal lymph nodes. Urine Histoplasma antigen, Histoplasma immunodiffusion (H and M bands), Histoplasma mycelial and yeast complement fixation, serum Blastomyces antigen and antibody, serum Aspergillus antibody, serum Coccidioides antibody, and serum HIV antigen/antibody were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial and repeat shave biopsies of the left infraorbital plaque demonstrated granulomatous inflammation with pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and numerous intracellular/extracellular narrow-based budding yeast forms highlighted by PAS and Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver (GMS) stains and negative on Fontana-Masson and mucicarmine stains (excluding Cryptococcus). Illumina iSeq100 next-generation sequencing (NGS) of a 230-bp internal transcribed spacer (ITS) amplicon from the formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue block definitively identified Histoplasma capsulatum.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Primary/isolated recurrent cutaneous histoplasmosis of the left infraorbital cheek mimicking nonmelanoma skin cancer in an immunocompetent host, definitively confirmed by PAS and GMS histopathology and FFPE tissue block ITS next-generation sequencing identifying Histoplasma capsulatum despite negative serum and urine Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Coccidioides, and Aspergillus serologies/antigens. Treated with oral itraconazole 200 mg daily for a planned 1-year course, with complete clearance and no recurrence at 8-month follow-up.
